listing_basis: CITES Appendices in force from 5 March 2026 (amendments adopted at CoP20, Samarkand, 24 Nov - 5 Dec 2025), checked against the Species+ export of 2026-10-22.
changes: Podocarpus parlatorei transferred from Appendix I to Appendix II with a zero export quota for wild-taken specimens for commercial purposes (in force 5 March 2026).
Paubrasilia echinata (pernambuco) stays in Appendix II with a revised annotation #10 and a zero quota for wild-harvested specimens in commercial trade.
Proposals to remove Central African populations of Afzelia bipindensis and Pterocarpus soyauxii from Appendix II were rejected: both stay listed.
Commiphora wightii (guggul, a resin tree, not timber) added to Appendix II with annotation #19.
Platymiscium pleiostachyum is now listed under the name Platymiscium parviflorum.
disclaimer: Macroscopic identification is a screening tool, usually reliable only to genus or group. Confirm with an accredited wood-anatomy, DNA or mass-spectrometry laboratory and the live Species+ listing before enforcement action.

#1.plain: All parts and derivatives, except seeds/spores/pollen, seedlings or tissue cultures in vitro, cut flowers of artificially propagated plants (timber, finished goods covered).
#1.official: All parts and derivatives, except: a) seeds, spores and pollen (including pollinia); b) seedling or tissue cultures obtained in vitro transported in sterile containers; c) cut flowers of artificially propagated plants; and d) fruits, and parts and derivatives thereof, of artificially propagated plants of the genus Vanilla

#2.plain: All parts and derivatives except seeds and pollen, and finished products packaged and ready for retail trade.
#2.official: All parts and derivatives except: a) seeds and pollen; and b) finished products packaged and ready for retail trade

#4.plain: All parts and derivatives except seeds, spores and pollen, in-vitro seedling/tissue cultures, cut flowers of artificially propagated plants and a few plant-specific items (certain Vanilla, Cactaceae, Opuntia/Selenicereus stems, finished Euphorbia antisyphilitica products). For timber: logs, sawn wood, veneer, plywood, chips AND finished products ARE covered.
#4.official: All parts and derivatives, except: a) seeds (including seedpods of Orchidaceae), spores and pollen (including pollinia). The exemption does not apply to seeds from Cactaceae spp. exported from Mexico, and to seeds from Beccariophoenix madagascariensis and Dypsis decaryi exported from Madagascar; b) seedling or tissue cultures obtained in vitro transported in sterile containers; c) cut flowers of artificially propagated plants; d) fruits, and parts and derivatives thereof, of naturalized or artificially propagated plants of the genus Vanilla (Orchidaceae) and of the family Cactaceae; e) stems, flowers, and parts and derivatives thereof, of naturalized or artificially propagated plants of the genera Opuntia subgenus Opuntia and Selenicereus (Cactaceae); f) finished products packaged and ready for retail trade of Aloe ferox and Euphorbia antisyphilitica; and g) finished products derived from artificial propagation, packaged and ready for retail trade of cosmetics containing parts and derivatives of Bletilla striata, Cycnoches cooperi, Gastrodia elata, Phalaenopsis amabilis or Phalaenopsis lobbii.

#5.plain: Logs, sawn wood and veneer sheets.
#5.official: Logs, sawn wood and veneer sheets

#6.plain: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets and plywood.
#6.official: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets and plywood.

#7.plain: Logs, wood chips, powder and extracts.

#10.plain: All parts and derivatives, except finished musical instruments, accessories and parts moved NON-commercially (performance, personal use, display, loan, competition, teaching, appraisal, repair) without change of ownership. Zero quota for wild-harvested specimens (source W) traded commercially. Bows, bow blanks, logs and sawn wood in commercial trade ARE covered.
#10.official: All parts and derivatives, except finished musical instruments, finished musical instrument accessories and finished musical instrument parts for non-commercial trade only for the purpose of paid and unpaid performance, personal use, display, loan, competition, teaching, appraisal, or repair, provided that this does not change the ownership and that such transport is not for sale, transfer or disposal of the specimen outside of the owner's usual State of residence. Zero quota for wild-harvested specimens (source code W) traded for commercial purposes.

#11.plain: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood, powder and extracts (finished products containing extracts as ingredients are exempt).
#11.official: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood, powder and extracts. Finished products containing such extracts as ingredients, including fragrances, are not considered to be covered by this annotation.

#12.plain: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood and extracts.
#12.official: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood and extracts. Finished products containing such extracts as ingredients, including fragrances, are not considered to be covered by this annotation

#14.plain: All parts and derivatives except seeds/pollen, seedling cultures, fruits, leaves, exhausted agarwood powder and finished retail products (agarwood chips, oil, powder ARE covered).
#14.official: All parts and derivatives except: a) seeds and pollen; b) seedling or tissue cultures obtained in vitro transported in sterile containers; c) fruits; d) leaves; e) exhausted agarwood powder, including compressed powder in all shapes; and f) finished products packaged and ready for retail trade, this exemption does not apply to wood chips, beads, prayer beads and carvings.

#15.plain: All parts and derivatives except (a) leaves, flowers, pollen, fruits, seeds; (b) finished products up to 10 kg wood of listed species per shipment; (c) finished musical instruments, parts and accessories; (d) D. cochinchinensis (covered by #4); (e) Dalbergia spp. from Mexico (covered by #6).
#15.official: All parts and derivatives, except: a) Leaves, flowers, pollen, fruits, and seeds; b) Finished products to a maximum weight of wood of the listed species of up to 10 kg per shipment; c) Finished musical instruments, finished musical instrument parts and finished musical instrument accessories; d) Parts and derivatives of Dalbergia cochinchinensis, which are covered by Annotation # 4; and e) Parts and derivatives of Dalbergia spp. originating and exported from Mexico, which are covered by Annotation # 6.

#16.plain: Seeds, fruits and oils (Adansonia grandidieri) - not timber.

#19.plain: Extracts (resins, gums, essential oils) and powder, except finished products packaged and ready for retail trade (Commiphora wightii, listed at CoP20) - not timber.
#19.official: Extracts (including resins, gums and essential oils) and powder, except the following finished products, packaged and ready for retail trade: finished tablets, capsules, pills, perfumes, cosmetics, solutions, emulsions or suspensions (such as infused oils, hydrolates, tinctures), and manufactured incense products (such as incense sticks and incense cones).

taxa.range: Atlantic coastal forest of eastern Brazil (Bahia to Minas Gerais / Espírito Santo).
taxa.heartwood: Dark chocolate-brown to purplish/reddish brown with irregular black streaks (spider-web figure); oily feel.
taxa.odour: Distinct sweet, rose-like scent when freshly cut.

endgrain.deposits: dark red-brown gum in some pores
special: Parenchyma forms fine wavy tangential bands and lozenge-aliform patches around pores

taxa.key_diagnostic: Dark heartwood with black streaks + rose scent + medium pores (few, solitary/short multiples) + banded/aliform parenchyma + very fine rays. Cannot be separated reliably from other Dalbergia (esp. D. spruceana, D. latifolia) by hand lens alone.
taxa.lab_methods: Fluorescence of ethanol extract, DART-TOF mass spectrometry and DNA have been used to separate D. nigra from look-alikes; macroscopic ID = genus level only.

taxa.population_scope: All species except D. nigra (App. I). D. cochinchinensis = #4; Mexican populations = #6.
taxa.range: Pantropical: Central & South America, Africa, Madagascar, South & Southeast Asia (c. 250-300 species).
taxa.heartwood: Very variable: purple-brown, red-orange, chocolate, nearly black; often streaked.
taxa.odour: Many species fragrant (rose, spicy, sweet) when cut or sanded.

endgrain.deposits: red-brown to black gum in some pores
special: Rays and parenchyma storied: ripple marks often visible on tangential face
Fine, regularly spaced parenchyma bands (sometimes wavy) between pores
Rays very fine - barely visible even at 10x

taxa.key_diagnostic: GENUS LEVEL: diffuse-porous, few medium/large pores, fine banded + aliform parenchyma, storied rays (ripple marks), dark often fragrant heartwood. Treat any wood matching this pattern as SUSPECT Dalbergia (CITES App II) until proven otherwise.
lookalikes: Machaerium spp. (pau ferro, Bolivian rosewood - NOT listed)
taxa.lab_methods: DART-TOF mass spectrometry, NIR spectroscopy and DNA barcoding are used to reach species level; macroscopic = genus/group.

taxa.scientific_name: Swietenia macrophylla, S. humilis, S. mahagoni
taxa.annotation: S. macrophylla #6 (Neotropical populations); S. humilis #4; S. mahagoni #5
taxa.population_scope: S. macrophylla: Neotropics only (plantations in Asia/Fiji not covered)
taxa.range: Mexico through Central America to the Amazon (S. macrophylla); Pacific dry forest of Mexico-Costa Rica (S. humilis); Caribbean & Florida (S. mahagoni).
taxa.heartwood: Light pinkish to deep reddish-brown, darkening; lustrous with ribbon figure.

endgrain.deposits: dark red-brown gum and/or white deposits in some pores
special: Distinct pale lines of marginal (terminal) parenchyma delimit growth rings
Ripple marks frequently present on tangential face
Rays visible at 10x, reddish

taxa.key_diagnostic: Diffuse-porous reddish wood with medium pores (solitary + short radial multiples), white or dark gum deposits, distinct marginal parenchyma lines and frequent ripple marks.
lookalikes: Khaya spp. (African mahogany - usually no ripple marks, often no marginal lines)
taxa.lab_methods: Microscopy separates Swietenia from Khaya (ray structure, crystals); DNA/MS for species.
